Given Soda may be promo-inflated, apply a 0.6 weight to Soda for both clusters to control for discount-driven volume. Recompute weighted totals as: sum(all except Soda) + 0.6 * Soda.

```python
import pandas as pd

file_path = '/Data2/v-weilinjin/workshop/AttributeBench/benchmarks/GAIA/2023/validation/7cc4acfa-63fd-4acc-a1a1-e8e529e0a97f.xlsx'
df = pd.read_excel(file_path)

sales_cols_no_soda = ['Burgers', 'Hot Dogs', 'Salads', 'Fries', 'Ice Cream']

cluster_al = ['Algrimand', 'Pinebrook', 'Sagrada']
cluster_wh = ['Wharvton']

al_no_soda = df[df['Location'].isin(cluster_al)][sales_cols_no_soda].sum().sum()
al_soda = df[df['Location'].isin(cluster_al)]['Soda'].sum()
wh_no_soda = df[df['Location'].isin(cluster_wh)][sales_cols_no_soda].sum().sum()
wh_soda = df[df['Location'].isin(cluster_wh)]['Soda'].sum()

al_weighted = al_no_soda + 0.6 * al_soda
wh_weighted = wh_no_soda + 0.6 * wh_soda

print('Weighted Totals (Soda weight=0.6):')
print('Algrimand cluster:', al_weighted)
print('Wharvton:', wh_weighted)
```
